children: European gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel prices in the region, drop more than 7% in afternoon trading after G-7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel from their emergency stocks. "We will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G-7 members and partners," they said in a statement. In afternoon trading, gasoil futures are down 7.3% to $1,342.25 a metric ton. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
